source: Boyd (1991) Strategic planning and financial performance: a meta-analytic review
finding: First meta-analysis of planning vs performance. Found only modest correlations. Authors say measurement problems mean the true link is underestimated.
numbers: 29 samples, 2496 organizations, nine performance measures. Abstract only; exact r not read.
agent_relevance: Planning pays modestly. Do not expect a big jump from planning alone.

source: Schwenk & Shrader (1993) Effects of formal strategic planning on financial performance in small firms: a meta-analysis
finding: Planning-performance link across small-firm studies is positive and significant, but individual effects are small. Much variance is not explained by sampling error, so moderators exist.
numbers: Abstract only; exact r and k not read.
agent_relevance: Average gain hides large variance. The agent should gate planning on context.

source: Capon, Farley & Hulbert (1994) Strategic planning and financial performance: more evidence
finding: Adds a Fortune 500 manufacturing study that Boyd omitted, plus longer follow-up on performance and firm survival. Small but positive link persists.
numbers: Abstract only: small positive relationship that persists over a longer period.
agent_relevance: Effect is small but durable, not a one-off.

source: Miller & Cardinal (1994) Strategic planning and firm performance: a synthesis of more than two decades of research
finding: Canonical meta-analytic synthesis of planning and performance. I could not read the abstract or text; only the bibliographic record was seen.
numbers: No numbers read. Crossref lists 603 citations.
agent_relevance: Treat as the canonical positive result; verify details before using numbers.

source: Armstrong (1982) The value of formal planning for strategic decisions: review of empirical research
finding: Formal planning beat informal in 10 of 15 comparisons drawn from 12 studies. Informal won in only 2. Mild support for stakeholder participation. Formal planning more useful where large changes were involved.
numbers: 10 of 15 formal better; 2 of 15 informal better; 12 studies (abstract).
limits: Few studies; little info on which parts of planning matter.
agent_relevance: Planning helps most under large change. Suggests structured option work on big decisions only.

source: Bracker & Pearson (1986) Planning and financial performance of small, mature firms
finding: Small mature firms with structured strategic plans did better financially than those without (MANOVA). Authors say it overcomes methodological flaws of earlier work.
numbers: Abstract only; no N or effect size read.
agent_relevance: Planning sophistication, not just having a plan, was the measured unit.

source: Bracker & Keats (1988) Planning and financial performance among small firms in a growth industry
finding: Replicated the small-firm result in a growth industry: sophisticated planners did better.
numbers: Abstract only; no figures read.
agent_relevance: Effect replicates across industry settings.

source: Rhyne (1986) The relationship of strategic planning to financial performance
finding: Planning systems that combined an external focus with a long-term perspective went with higher 10-year total return to stockholders. A lagged link to 4-year average annual returns was also found.
numbers: Abstract only; no figures read.
limits: Observational; reverse causation possible though a lag was tested.
agent_relevance: Content of planning matters: look outward and long-term, not just plan more.

source: Delmar & Shane (2003) Does business planning facilitate the development of new ventures?
finding: Business planning reduces the chance a venture disbands and speeds product development and organizing. Mechanism: helps founders decide, balance resources and turn goals into concrete steps.
numbers: 223 new Swedish ventures begun in first 9 months of 1998, random sample of founders (abstract).
agent_relevance: Mechanism is decision-making and turning goals into steps, as an agent plan does.

source: Hamann, Halw & Guenther (2022) Meta-analysis of the corporate planning-organizational performance relationship (SMJ)
finding: Latest meta-analysis. Planning correlates with performance; stable over time and across planning types. Manufacturing and larger firms gain more. High uncertainty-avoidance countries and high environmental uncertainty show bigger effects.
numbers: 183 independent samples, 84 examined for the first time. Corrects for measurement error and dichotomization (abstract). Full text blocked (403).
limits: Results conditional on how performance and planning are measured; unexpected interaction with uncertainty avoidance.
agent_relevance: Planning helps MORE under uncertainty, against the plans-fail-in-turbulence view. Supports planning on hard problems.

source: George, Walker & Monster (2019) Does strategic planning improve organizational performance? A meta-analysis (Public Administration Review)
finding: Random-effects meta-analysis: planning has a positive, moderate, significant effect on performance. Strongest when performance is effectiveness and planning is formal. Holds in public and private sectors and in US and non-US contexts.
numbers: 87 correlations from 31 studies (abstract). Wikipedia says almost 9,000 organizations. Full text blocked (403).
limits: Gain is largest for effectiveness (reaching goals).
agent_relevance: Planning raises goal achievement more than efficiency. For the agent: planning buys accuracy, not speed.

source: Wikipedia: Strategic planning (summary of George et al. 2019 and McKinsey 2006)
finding: Page reports the McKinsey 2006 survey found many firms had formal planning but did not use it for their most important decisions. Defines comprehensiveness as many options before selecting. Benefits depend on formality, comprehensiveness, stakeholder management.
numbers: No sample size or percentages for the McKinsey survey on the page. Meta-analysis described as almost 9,000 organizations.
limits: Secondary source; survey authors not named.
agent_relevance: Having a process is not the same as applying it to key decisions. The agent must route hard decisions through it.

source: Fredrickson & Mitchell (1984) Strategic decision processes: comprehensiveness and performance in an industry with an unstable environment
finding: Classic test of comprehensive decision process (many options, thorough analysis) in an unstable industry. Only the record was seen, no abstract.
numbers: No numbers read. Crossref lists 608 citations.
limits: I did not read the finding. It is often cited as a boundary condition (comprehensiveness vs instability) but that is unverified here.
agent_relevance: Candidate boundary condition for option generation; verify before relying on it.

source: Dean & Sharfman (1996) Does decision process matter? A study of strategic decision-making effectiveness
finding: Tests whether procedural rationality in strategic decisions predicts effectiveness. Only the record was seen, no abstract.
numbers: No numbers read. Crossref lists 691 citations.
agent_relevance: Check later: procedural rationality (information, analysis) vs decision effectiveness.

source: Brinckmann, Grichnik & Kapsa (2010) Should entrepreneurs plan or just storm the castle? Meta-analysis of contextual factors (J Business Venturing)
finding: Meta-analysis on contextual moderators of the planning-performance link in small firms. Abstract not available to me; only the title and record were seen.
numbers: No numbers read. Crossref lists 520 citations.
agent_relevance: Candidate source for small and new firm moderators.

source: Nutt (1993) The formulation processes and tactics used in organizational decision making
finding: 163 decision cases coded. Four formulation processes found: idea, issue, objective-directed, reframing. Success judged by adoption, merit and duration.
numbers: N = 163 cases. Abstract gives no success rates.
limits: Coded case studies, not an experiment.
agent_relevance: Compare formulation patterns with our S-states for framing.

source: Camuffo, Cordova, Gambardella & Spina (2020) A scientific approach to entrepreneurial decision making: randomized control trial (Management Science)
finding: Startups trained to form hypotheses and test them performed better and pivoted more than controls, with no higher dropout. Theory: a scientific approach improves precision.
numbers: 116 Italian startups, 16 data points over about one year. Both groups got 10 sessions of general training (abstract).
limits: Treatment was hypothesis testing, not planning as such.
agent_relevance: Best causal evidence that structured predict-and-test beats intuition. Matches test-before-commit (G3).

source: Clear and present danger: planning and new venture survival amid political and civil violence (SMJ 2014)
finding: In violent environments, incremental operational planning helped survival more, and comprehensive strategic planning helped less.
numbers: 730 new ventures in Colombia, 1997 to 2001 (abstract).
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: comprehensive planning loses value in severe instability; short-horizon planning keeps value.

source: Kahneman & Lovallo (1993) Timid choices and bold forecasts
finding: Inside view anchors predictions on plans and scenarios and makes forecasts overly optimistic. Treating each problem as unique ignores past statistics.
numbers: Abstract only; no figures.
agent_relevance: Plans themselves cause overconfidence. Compare a plan to base rates (outside view).

source: Wikipedia: Planning fallacy (Buehler, Griffin & Ross)
finding: People underestimate the time their own plans take.
numbers: 37 students: estimated 33.9 days (best case 27.4, worst case 48.6); actual 55.5 days; about 30% finished within prediction. 1995 study: 13% finished by their 50% date, 19% by 75%, 45% by 99%.
agent_relevance: Planning raises confidence faster than accuracy. Discount confidence after planning.

source: Wikipedia: Business plan
finding: Page holds no empirical evidence that business plans improve performance. Only a practitioner claim and a note that costs are underestimated and revenues overestimated.
numbers: No sample sizes or rates.
agent_relevance: Popular claims for planning often lack data; lean on the meta-analyses.

source: Wikipedia: Strategic management (Mintzberg, Ansoff)
finding: Mintzberg 1988 found the strategic process fluid and could not identify one process called strategic planning. Strategy can be intended or emergent. Rival view to planning.
numbers: No performance figures; one 1979 study: 45% of Fortune 500 used the growth-share matrix.
limits: First 100,000 characters of the page read.
agent_relevance: Rival theory: emergent strategy. Allow plan revision on real feedback; no rigid plans.

source: Doshi, Bell, Mirzayev & Vanneste (2024) Generative AI and evaluating strategic decisions (SMJ)
finding: LLM evaluations of business models were inconsistent and biased singly. Aggregating across LLMs, prompts and roles made AI rankings resemble human experts.
numbers: Two studies, 60 business models each, compared with human expert rankings (abstract). Correlations not read.
agent_relevance: Supports selection by aggregation in code (G5), not one model judgment.

source: Girotra, Meincke, Terwiesch & Ulrich (2023) Ideas are dimes a dozen: LLMs for idea generation in innovation
finding: ChatGPT-4 made ideas faster and cheaper than elite-university students, with higher average quality (purchase intent) and higher variance. Most of the best ideas in the pooled sample came from ChatGPT.
numbers: Abstract only; counts not read. Few-shot examples of highly rated ideas raised performance further.
limits: Idea quality by purchase-intent survey, not firm performance.
agent_relevance: Option generation is cheap for an LLM; the bottleneck is picking the best of many.

source: Cristofaro & Giardino (2026) Generative AI and cognitive biases in strategic decision-making
finding: Randomized lab experiment: intermediate GenAI use gave lower anchoring, confirmation and overconfidence. Low and high use were worse. Critical interrogation of outputs was the active ingredient.
numbers: 273 business professionals; time-constrained, high-uncertainty market-entry task (abstract).
limits: Humans using AI; not an autonomous agent.
agent_relevance: Too little and too much model output both hurt. Comparing and challenging alternatives matters.

source: Vending-Bench: long-horizon coherence of LLM agents running a vending business (arXiv 2502.15840)
finding: LLM agents running a simulated vending business had huge run-to-run variance. Failures were misread deliveries, forgotten orders and tangential meltdowns, not memory limits.
numbers: Mean net worth over 5 runs: Claude 3.5 Sonnet $2,217.93 (min $476), o3-mini $906.86, human (1 run) $844.05, Gemini 1.5 Pro $594.02, GPT-4o $335.46. Start balance $500. Sonnet mean 1,560 units sold but min 0.
agent_relevance: Best models still collapse in some runs; need code-checked state tracking.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-consistency improves chain of thought reasoning (arXiv 2203.11171)
finding: Sampling many reasoning paths and taking the majority answer improves accuracy.
numbers: Absolute gains: GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2, StrategyQA +6.4, ARC-challenge +3.9.
limits: Needs one checkable answer; samples from one model are correlated.
agent_relevance: Many options plus code selection works when answers can be compared.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts (arXiv 2305.10601)
finding: Generating several candidate thoughts and searching over them beats a single chain on Game of 24.
numbers: Success over 100 games: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC (k=100) 9.0%, ToT breadth 1 = 45%, ToT breadth 5 = 74%. Best of 100 CoT samples reached 49%.
limits: Task allows evaluating partial states; GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Options plus evaluation of partial states beat the same compute spent on independent samples.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve prompting (arXiv 2305.04091)
finding: Asking the model first to devise a plan then execute gives modest gains over zero-shot CoT.
numbers: text-davinci-003 average over six math sets: zero-shot CoT 70.4, PS 73.5, PS+ 76.7; manual few-shot CoT 77.6. PS+ beat CoT by at least 5 points except GSM8K (+2.9).
agent_relevance: A plan step helps a little; detailed instructions help more.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2022) PlanBench (arXiv 2206.10498)
finding: LLMs were poor at actual plan generation in Blocksworld and at verifying plans.
numbers: GPT-4 plan generation 206/600 (34.3%); Instruct-GPT3 41/600 (6.8%). Plan verification GPT-4 191/600 (31.8%), Instruct-GPT3 4/600 (0.6%).
agent_relevance: Models both plan and verify plans poorly; use an external verifier.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2024) LLMs still can't plan; can LRMs? o1 on PlanBench (arXiv 2409.13373)
finding: o1-preview greatly improved planning but is not robust, degrades with length, and is slow and costly versus a classical planner.
numbers: Mystery Blocksworld zero-shot: o1-preview 52.8% (317/600), o1-mini 19.1%; randomized mystery 37.3%. Fast Downward 100% in 0.265 s. Best plain LLM on Blocksworld 62.6% (Llama 3.1 405B).
agent_relevance: More thinking helps planning, but a code planner or verifier still wins.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLMs can't plan, but can help planning in LLM-Modulo frameworks (arXiv 2402.01817)
finding: Position paper: LLMs generate candidate plans but cannot reliably plan or self-verify; pair them with external model-based verifiers.
numbers: No new experiment figures taken from it.
agent_relevance: Supports our split: model proposes, program verifies and selects.

source: Huang et al. (2023) LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet (arXiv 2310.01798)
finding: Without external feedback, self-revision does not improve and sometimes degrades reasoning.
numbers: GSM8K, GPT-3.5 keeps its initial answer 74.7% of the time over two rounds; among changes, more correct-to-wrong than wrong-to-correct.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: revise a plan only from real output.

source: Plan-and-Act (arXiv 2503.09572)
finding: A separate planner plus executor with dynamic replanning raised web-agent success.
numbers: WebArena-Lite (165 test tasks): base executor 9.85%; adding a base planner 29.63%; with dynamic replanning 57.58% (state of the art when published).
limits: Trained planner on synthetic data; benchmark-specific.
agent_relevance: Explicit planning plus replanning on observed state gave the largest agent gains found.

source: TheAgentCompany (arXiv 2412.14161)
finding: LLM agents doing simulated company tasks fully complete under a third of them.
numbers: Best: Gemini 2.5 Pro 30.3% full completion, 39.3% score; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 24.0%; Qwen-2.5-72b 5.7%.
agent_relevance: Real business-like tasks remain hard.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking (arXiv 2506.06941)
finding: On puzzles with controlled complexity, reasoning models show three regimes and a complete accuracy collapse past a critical complexity; reasoning effort falls near collapse.
numbers: Qualitative from text read; no single headline number taken.
agent_relevance: Boundary: extra deliberation helps in a middle band only. Match planning effort to difficulty.

source: Costarelli et al. (2024) GameBench (arXiv 2406.06613)
finding: Strategic game benchmark: no tested model matched human performance; CoT and RAP raised scores but not to human level.
numbers: GPT-4 with CoT best model, below human baseline, above random baseline.
agent_relevance: Strategic reasoning gap to humans persists even with scaffolds.
